clue.text: Whittington's pet food?

parts.note: Dick Whittington, the pantomime Lord Mayor of London, had a famous cat; what would its dinner be? Read the other way, it names a creature of the sea

explanation.surface: A question about what Dick Whittington's famous companion ate.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Whittington is the hero of a British pantomime whose cat made his fortune. A cat's food is fish, and putting the two words together gives a whiskered fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The catfish is a whiskered fish, and fish is just what a cat would eat.

clue.text: One of the biggest fiddlers on record?

definitions.text: One of the biggest fiddlers on record?

parts.words: One of the biggest fiddlers on record?
parts.note: a fiddler sounds like a cheat on the books, but here it plays a large stringed instrument, bigger than a violin, maybe for a recording

explanation.surface: A notorious fraudster in the record books.
explanation.definitionFit: The player of a large bowed string instrument plays one bigger than the violin.

clue.text: Palm-tree cut, chopped — treat with contempt

indicators.note: chopped up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
cut short, so the last letter is lopped off

explanation.surface: A palm tree felled and hacked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the final E from PALMTREE, and 'chopped' rearranges what is left, PALMTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample on someone's feelings is to disregard them with scorn.

clue.text: Not much land, in the main, but somebody's leased it

definitions.text: Not much land, in the main

explanation.surface: A small piece of sea-bound land rented out to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two words, IS LET: somebody has leased it, so it is let.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny island is a small bit of land in the sea (the main), and a property rented out is let.

clue.text: The type to take silly risks with ice-caps?

definitions.text: The type to take silly risks with ice-caps?

parts.words: The type to take silly risks with ice-caps?
parts.note: a reckless person needs cooling down, and ice caps worn on the head would cool a fevered head

explanation.surface: A question about the reckless sort and polar ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rash and impetuous takes foolish chances; literally they need ice packs on the head to cool it.

clue.text: His man lacking polish, gets cut

definitions.note: one of Christ's men, i.e. an apostle and evangelist

parts.note: a matt finish is dull, without gloss or shine
to hew is to cut with an axe or blade

explanation.surface: A rough, unpolished servant gets a slash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' (capitalised as the first word) refers to Christ: one of His men is an apostle, here the gospel writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The tax collector of the Gospels became one of the twelve apostles, a follower of Jesus.

clue.text: A horse for Snowdon?

explanation.surface: Choosing a horse to ride up the Welsh peak.
explanation.walkthrough: Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider's horse is a steed, and a mountain is a mount in its names, like Mount Everest.

clue.text: Yet he could be a fathead, not keeping his hair on!

definitions.text: Yet he could be a fathead, not keeping his hair on!

parts.words: Yet he could be a fathead, not keeping his hair on!
parts.note: keeping one's hair on means staying calm, but here it means literally losing hair, while fathead is read as a fat head, the opposite of slim

explanation.surface: An idiot losing his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A balding man has sparse hair on his head, which can still be a fat one.

clue.text: Top places for which he adjusted sight

indicators.note: adjusting rearranges, so the letters of the word sight are reordered

explanation.surface: A climber adjusts his view to reach the summits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for which' is only a link; 'adjusted' is the anagram signal working on 'sight', not a spectacle fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: High points and summits are lofty places.

clue.text: Short general holiday with a pronouncedly feeble conclusion

indicators.note: said out loud, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a feeble conclusion is a weak end

explanation.surface: A brief break that fizzles out at its close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronouncedly' signals a homophone: WEAK END said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saturday-Sunday break is a short rest from work taken by most people.

clue.text: A tract twigged?

parts.note: a tract is a printed pamphlet; with the question mark the clue also asks for something sprouting on a twig, a small leaf

explanation.definitionFit: A pamphlet handed out is a printed handbill, and in botany the same word names a small leaf on a stalk or twig.

clue.text: Patchwork suit Eli put to some purpose

indicators.note: patchwork pieces scraps together in a new pattern, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eli made patchwork out of an old suit to give it a use.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ something is to make it serve a purpose.

clue.text: I'm on the sick list and can't wait to get off it

definitions.text: can't wait to get off it

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
someone under a doctor's care is a patient

explanation.surface: A hospital invalid who is longing to be discharged.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the sick list: the patient can't wait to be off it, and 'can't wait' is the adjective's whole sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless and eager who cannot bear delay cannot wait.

clue.text: Mixed hue from pibroch revelries

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of these words, spanning the word join

explanation.surface: A colour emerging from wild Highland bagpipe merrymaking.
explanation.walkthrough: A pibroch is a piece of Scottish bagpipe music.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellowish-brown earth pigment is a colour made by mixing clay and iron oxide.

clue.text: Twitch pulled out at Kew

indicators.note: pulled out of shape, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone twitches after being dragged out at Kew Gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled out' rearranges AT and KEW. Kew is the botanical gardens in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a sharp pull or twitch.

clue.text: Make sure there's enough to refill the shelves

definitions.text: Make sure there's enough to refill the shelves

parts.words: Make sure there's enough to refill the shelves
parts.note: a shopkeeper holds supplies in reserve, so goods are on hand for the empty shelves

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper ensures supplies to restock shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding reserves of goods in a shop ensures supply.

clue.text: Temporarily managed in somebody'else's shoes?

parts.note: to stand in another's shoes is to take their place; running things for a while in their stead is acting as a stand-in

explanation.surface: Someone briefly runs things while filling a colleague's role.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as a substitute for an absent person is to stand in for them.

clue.text: Before the time is ripe?

parts.note: the phrase means too early, and mature also means ripe, so this is before ripeness

explanation.definitionFit: Something happening too early comes ahead of its proper time, literally before maturity.

clue.text: A precarious position for the grinder's work?

explanation.surface: A knife grinder's trade is a risky one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a tense, uncertain balance is a precarious state, and a grinder sharpens the honed sharp side of a blade.

clue.text: Get rid of your boots? But the match has just started

explanation.surface: A footballer pulls off their boots, yet the game has only just begun.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick off one's shoes is to remove them with a flick, and the kick-off is the moment a football game begins.

clue.text: The sluggish state of one injured retina

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: an injured eye part is damaged, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with an injured eye is left sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' gives the Roman numeral I, and 'injured' is the anagram signal for 'retina'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy and a lack of energy or movement make a sluggish state.

clue.text: Some ballroom footwear makes for persistent questions

explanation.surface: Dance shoes that keep firing questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Light dancing shoes go by this name, and to interrogate someone persistently is to pump them for information.

clue.text: Martin's market permit

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is': the definition is martin, the bird

parts.note: a mart is a market
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A man called Martin has a licence to trade at market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Martin' looks like a man's name; it is the swallow-like bird, and the 's reads as 'is'. A martlet is a martin, or in heraldry a footless bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This old word names the house martin or swift, a swallow-like bird.

clue.text: Dubbed a cut above the average joint

parts.note: a man dubbed by the sovereign is knighted, and becomes Sir
a loin is a joint of meat

explanation.surface: A knighted fellow is a cut above the ordinary roast.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says a king knighted a loin of beef. The definition is a superior cut of meat, a cut above the average.
explanation.definitionFit: This beef steak from the upper loin is a choice, superior piece of meat.

clue.text: Thirty two men compete for places on the board

definitions.text: Thirty two men compete for places on the board

parts.words: Thirty two men compete for places on the board
parts.note: the board sounds like a company boardroom, but the thirty-two men are the pieces of a game played on squares

explanation.surface: Thirty-two candidates jostle for seats as company directors.
explanation.definitionFit: The game is played with thirty-two pieces, called men, moving on a chequered board.

clue.text: Rare pelts somehow smoother

indicators.note: in some unspecified way, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unusual animal skins are somehow softer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges RARE PELTS. 'Smoother' looks like a comparative adjective but is one who smooths walls.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who coats walls in a smooth finish is a wall-smoother.

clue.text: A prodder at the gaming table

explanation.surface: Someone nudging players at the casino.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire iron prods coals, and the card game of bluff is played at the gaming table.

clue.text: Balking at ark the otter brought to book

indicators.note: balking means jibbing or shying away, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: An otter refusing to board the ark, then written up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balking' rearranges AT ARK. Henry Williamson's novel 'Tarka the Otter' is the book in which the otter is portrayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Williamson's novel stars an otter of this name, an otter put in print.

clue.text: What's likely to happen when caught, perhaps, by a glance

parts.note: in cricket, being caught is one way of being out
a look is a brief glance

explanation.surface: Predictions made when someone is spotted at a glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught, perhaps' is a cricket dismissal, a batter is out.
explanation.definitionFit: The prospect for the future is what is expected to come.

clue.text: Disastrous tour broken by sick painter

indicators.note: the rearranged word is split open with the other piece set inside
a disastrous outing wrecks things, so the letters of the word tour are rearranged

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A bad trip interrupted by illness for an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disastrous' scrambles 'tour' and 'broken by' splits that scramble round the synonym for sick. Maurice Utrillo was a French painter of Paris street scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Utrillo was a French artist known for Montmartre street scenes.

clue.text: More honest postal worker cancelling the stamps

explanation.surface: A more candid post-office clerk marking the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank means candid, so more candid is the comparative; and one who franks mail marks its stamps as used.

clue.text: The stretchy protein of note Stalin decoded

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: decoding scrambles and reorders the code, so the letters of the dictator's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A secret note from Stalin is decrypted, revealing a scientific term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decoded' is the anagram signal for the dictator's name; the note comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: This protein gives skin and blood vessels their springiness and elasticity.
